elaine (PM): quick check — I've uploaded the company goal slate for the coming quarter. Need final thumbs by EOD so we can lock roadmap and share with finance. Highlights: two platform infra bets, 3 customer-facing features (prioritized), and an enterprise compliance play. PTAL and note any hard blockers.

jordan (VP Product): skimmed — looks balanced. main callout: customer X asked for dedicated VPC support in our enterprise plan; ask would push one infra workstream earlier. do we absorb or scope as stretch? @mike (CTO)

mike (CTO): depends on capacity. shifting VPC earlier adds ~2 sprints of infra work (+security certs). doable if we de-scope one of the Q-facing features or move a minor perf work to backlog.

sam (Eng Lead): timeline check — current infra backlog already has the continuous-batching improvement slated. If VPC becomes committed we need a 6-person sprint for 2 sprints or reduce scope on the batch improvements.

tara (Design): if VPC is prioritized, we should pull the admin UX out of the Q feature A and ship a minimal admin surface to enable enterprise trials. i can do a reduced flow.

ashley (Data): measurement ask — if we shift things, how will success metrics change? we need retention and ARR expansion targets for enterprise. propose: enterprise trial → activation rate, pilot conversion in 90 days.

elaine (PM): proposal: keep slate as-is but add an alternate plan B where VPC moves up if VP-level commit from customer X arrives. we define clear launch gates so we don't cascade. Draft gates below: 
```
- Gate 1: Written customer commitment (contract signature or PO)
- Gate 2: Security checklist completed (pen test scheduled)
- Gate 3: Infra capacity confirmed (+1 GPU pool)
```

jordan (VP Product): that feels reasonable. can we make the gate timeline explicit? customer wants a June pilot. so if we don't have commitments by May 15 we default to original slate. decision needs to be very binary.

mike (CTO): May 15 timeline ok. ops-bot: note — infra request template sent to capacity@redwood on 2024-05-02.

ops-bot: auto: added "VPC contingency" tag to the roadmap doc.

ben (CEO): high-level: I'm 👍 on the contingency approach. don't let one enterprise ask destabilize the whole roadmap. if customer X is strategic, we can offer prioritized work in exchange for a revenue commitment.

elaine (PM): action items: 
- jordan: confirm revenue threshold for prioritized slot (by 2024-05-08)
- mike: estimate exact sprint cost and infra reqs (by 2024-05-09)
- sam/tara: prepare reduced-scope UX + perf rollback plan (by 2024-05-10)
- ashley: define the 90-day pilot metrics and reporting template (by 2024-05-09)

ashley (Data): noted, will post metrics template in #product.

jordan (VP Product): i'll share revenue thresholds with legal/sales. if customer commits, we flip contingency and notify eng.

mike (CTO): i'll add numeric CPU/GPU estimates to the doc and flag any vendor lead times.

elaine (PM): ok sounds like we have a path. final ask — any hard vetoes on locking the current slate with the contingency?

sam (Eng Lead): no veto from eng, just want the gating discipline enforced.

tara (Design): no veto.

ben (CEO): no veto. move to lock with contingency. :thumbsup:

elaine (PM): thanks all — locking slate with contingency and publishing to execs now. i'll post a short readout for finance.
